description: Classify a single IPv4 or IPv6 address: whether it belongs to a VPN, a residential, datacenter, mobile or public proxy, a Tor node, a privacy relay or web gateway, a hosting provider or a CDN, with the provider name where we have one; whether a crawler or other bot uses it, and whose; whether it is anycast, or a mobile carrier's or satellite operator's space; and whether an SSH, mail or web server or an open DNS resolver answered on it, or a BitTorrent client was seen on it. Pass the `User-Agent` a client at this address sent as `user_agent` to learn whether the address bears it out, which tells a real crawler from one forging its agent. Private and reserved addresses are answered locally, without calling the API. Always read `coverage.note` before concluding anything from a field that is not in the result.

ip.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 address to classify.

user_agent.description: The `User-Agent` a client at this address sent. The answer's `user_agent` then names the agent and says whether this address bears it out, so a crawler forging its agent reads `spoofed`. An answer without `user_agent` did not check the agent, which is no verdict either way.

name: lookup_ip

coverage.description: Which datasets this result covered. Read `note` before interpreting any absent field.

result.description:
The union of every tier's answer. Every answer carries `ip`, `is_bogon`,
`is_vpn`, the Tor and relay members, `is_anycast`, `hostname`, `location` and
`asn`, with or without a key;
each remaining field is present when your tier includes it, and absent
otherwise. A client that must work across plans should treat an absent
flag as unknown rather than as `false`.

abuse.description:
Where to report abuse from the address, from our IP Abuse Contact
database. On a paid plan. Every key is present whenever the object is: empty
strings where no record covers the address.

email.description: Where to report abuse from the address.

network.description: The registry block it was derived from.

validated.description: ARIN reports the contact answered its yearly validation.

asn.description:
The autonomous system that announces the address. Every answer, with or
without a key.
Each field is present whenever the object is: `asn` is 0 and the rest
empty where no announcement covers the address.
The AS number, 0 when no announcement covers the address.

country.description: The country the AS's registry assigned it to.

domain.description: The AS operator's own registrable domain.

name.description: Name of the organization that operates the AS.

prefix.description: The announced BGP prefix that covers the address, the most specific when several do.

rpki_status.description: The announcement's RPKI status: valid, invalid or not_found.

type.description: The kind of network the AS runs: isp, hosting, education, government or business.

bittorrent.description: Detail for `is_bittorrent`. Empty when false. On a paid plan.

clients.description: The two-letter codes its clients name themselves by.

first_seen.description: The first day a client was seen here.

id_matches_ip.description: A client here derived its node ID from the address (BEP 42).

indexer.description: A DHT indexer rather than people.

last_reachable.description: The last day one answered, empty when none did.

verified.description: A client here answered, or two or more reported it at once.

bot.description: Detail for `is_bot`. Empty when false. On a paid plan.

agents.description: The bots the address serves, as their user agents name them (`Googlebot`, `GPTBot`); for an address that is not verified, the bots it claimed to be. One address can serve several, and `[]` means none is named.

categories.description: What those bots do: `search_engine`, `ai_training`, `ai_search`, `ai_assistant`, `ai_agent`, `seo`, `ads`, `preview`, `feed`, `monitoring`, `archiver`, `scanner`, `link_security`, `webhook` or `other`; `[]` where unknown.

confidence.description: `high`, `medium` or `low`: how sure we are the address is what the row says.

first_seen.description: The first day the address was seen as such.

identity.description: `verified` (the operator vouches for the address), `declared` (it names itself a bot that cannot be verified), `spoofed` (it claimed a bot whose operator vouches for other addresses) or `undeclared` (it hides as a browser and behaves as automation).

provider.description: The bot operator's ID; for an address that is not verified, the operator its claim named. Empty where no operator is known.

provider_name.description: That operator's name, empty where no operator is known.

verified.description: Whether the operator vouches for the address, so the bots in `agents` really are its.

verified_by.description: How a verified address verified: `list` (the operator publishes it), `rdns` (its reverse DNS name ends in a suffix the operator documents and resolves back) or `owner` (the operator's own space, seen claiming its bot); empty when not verified.

cap_reached.description:
On every answer to a key on a paid plan, and on no other: `false`
while the answer has every field, `true` once its organization's
overage cap is reached and the answer has Unlimited's. Lookups
answered past the cap are not billed; raising or removing the cap in
Billing turns it `false` again.

carrier.description: Detail for `is_carrier`. Empty when false. On a paid plan.

cdn.description: Detail for `is_cdn`. Empty when false. On a paid plan.

confidence.description: How strongly the classification is supported.

last_seen.description: The most recent date this address was observed in this dataset.

provider.description: The provider's ID, or an empty string where the dataset has none.

provider_name.description:
The name the provider catalog gives the provider; an empty string where the
catalog names none or the dataset has no provider.

company.description:
Who uses the address, from our IP Company database. On a paid plan. Every
key is present whenever the object is: empty strings where no record
covers the address.

type.description: What kind of organization: hosting, isp, business, education or government.

dcproxy.description: Detail for `is_dcproxy`. Empty when false. On a paid plan.

hits.description:
How many times the address was observed in the pool during the
window, as of its last day in it once it has left.

hits_days_pct.description:
The percentage of days in the window on which the address was seen,
as of its last day in it once it has left. A high value means a

last_seen.description:

hostname.description: The name the address's reverse DNS (PTR) record points to, from our IP RDNS database; an empty string when it has none. Every answer, with or without a key.

ip.description: The address that was looked up, normalized.

is_anycast.description: Whether the address is announced from many places at once, as a public DNS resolver's or a CDN's edge is. Every answer, with or without a key.

is_bittorrent.description: Whether a BitTorrent client was seen on the address in the last 90 days. On a paid plan.

is_bogon.description:
Whether the address is reserved space (RFC 1918, loopback, link-local,
documentation ranges and their IPv6 equivalents), answered from the
address alone. Every answer, with or without a key.

is_bot.description: Whether an automated client uses the address, such as a search engine's or an AI company's crawler, an uptime monitor, an internet scanner or a webhook sender. `bot` says whose, what it does and whether its operator vouches for the address. Every answer, with or without a key.

is_carrier.description: Whether the address is a mobile carrier's, where many phones can share one address. On a paid plan.

is_cdn.description: Whether the address belongs to a CDN. On a paid plan.

is_dcproxy.description: Whether the address is one a datacenter proxy service sells or runs on, a proxy company's own ranges included. On a paid plan.

is_dns_resolver.description: Whether an open DNS resolver answered on the address. On a paid plan.

is_hosting.description: Whether the address belongs to a hosting or cloud provider. On a paid plan.

is_mobproxy.description: Whether the address was seen in a mobile proxy pool. On a paid plan.

is_pubproxy.description: Whether a public proxy, one anyone can connect through, listens on the address or sends its traffic out from it. On a paid plan.

is_relay.description: Whether the address is privacy relay or enterprise web gateway egress, such as iCloud Private Relay or Zscaler. Every answer, with or without a key.

is_resproxy.description: Whether the address was seen in a residential proxy pool. On a paid plan.

is_satellite.description: Whether the address is a satellite operator's. On a paid plan.

is_smtp.description: Whether a mail server answered on the address. On a paid plan.

is_ssh.description: Whether an SSH server answered on the address. On a paid plan.

is_tor.description: Whether the address is a Tor node. Every answer, with or without a key.

is_vpn.description:
Whether the address is VPN infrastructure. Keys off presence in the
VPN dataset, so an unattributed range with no provider is still
`true`.

is_web.description: Whether a web server answered on the address, on port 80 or 443. On a paid plan.

location.description:
Where the address is: the fields of our IP Country database on every
answer, with or without a key, and our IP Geolocation database's finer
ones on a paid plan. Each field your plan includes is present whenever
the object is, so an address in no country, or a private one, answers
empty strings and zeros.

accuracy_radius.description: Radius in km holding the true location with 67% confidence; 20000 for an address announced everywhere, as an anycast one is. On a paid plan.

continent.description: Continent code: AF, AN (Antarctica), AS, EU, NA, OC or SA.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 code of the country's currency, where there is one.

currency_name.description: Name of the country's currency, where there is one.

currency_symbol.description: Symbol of the country's currency, where known.

dma_code.description: US TV market (DMA) code, empty outside the US. On a paid plan.

flag_emoji.description: The country's flag, as an emoji.

flag_unicode.description: The Unicode code points of the flag emoji.

geoname_id.description: GeoNames ID of the city. On a paid plan.

postal_code.description: Postal code. On a paid plan.

region.description: Region (state or province). On a paid plan.

verdict.description:
`verified`: the agent's operator vouches for this address as it.
`spoofed`: the operator of a bot that publishes its addresses, or
whose registered space it uses, does not vouch for this one, or this
address posed as the bot before. `unverifiable`: a bot no published
list or registered space can confirm. `not_bot`: a browser, an app or
a script. Known values: `verified`, `spoofed`, `unverifiable`, `not_bot`; the API may add more.
